prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to remove disease-relevant proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a new chemical principle, event-driven rather than occupancy-driven pharmacology, and it is the topic six of eight members placed in their top three at opening. The mechanism is not speculative: ternary-complex structures and the cereblon-thalidomide mechanism show how a small molecule reshapes an E3 ligase surface and brings a neomorphic substrate into contact. That is the structure-explains-function logic I value. Crews and Deshaies launched PROTACs and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, so a single prize can cover both the heterobifunctional and the molecular-glue arms. After two decades there is broad independent confirmation, many degraders in clinical trials, and approved glue-class drugs whose mechanism is now understood.
statement.case_against: Credit is the weak point: up to eight people are named, and a trio must leave out Ciulli (VHL ligands and structure-guided design), Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito. Handa's inclusion also rests on a mechanistic discovery about an existing drug rather than on a designed chemical tool, which makes the prize read as two lineages stitched together. Clinical proof for PROTACs specifically is still maturing, so a few years of waiting would carry little cost.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks Gray and Winkler's long-range electron transfer first, as a stable and overdue mechanistic result, and rates degradation as possibly early because no PROTAC is approved.
responses.response: I agree the electron-transfer work is rigorous and that its evidence base is complete. My reservation is breadth: it explains a mechanism in biophysics but has opened fewer new experiments and tools for chemists than induced proximity has. On maturity, lenalidomide-class glues are approved and their mechanism is understood, so the principle is clinically validated even though no PROTAC has yet been approved. I would treat B025 as a serious alternative for a later year, not as a reason to delay B014.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling first as a ubiquitous, mechanistically clean method with an unambiguous two-person credit, and ranks degradation sixth as perhaps a few years early.
responses.response: The clean attribution and daily use of C-N coupling are real strengths and I do not dispute them. My difficulty is that it extends the 2010 cross-coupling prize, so the question of a genuinely new chemical idea is harder to answer than for degradation. I also disagree that degradation is early: the PROTAC concept dates to 2001 and cereblon to 2010, and many laboratories have confirmed it. If the committee prefers the cleaner attribution, B057 is a defensible fallback and I would not oppose it, but I would not put it above B014 on novelty.

responses.point: Linke ranks degradation first and notes that the concept and first PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto) are separable from the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism (Handa, Ito).
responses.response: I agree with the separation, and it is why I include Handa and not Ciulli in my trio. I would argue that the two lineages meet at the same mechanism of E3 ligase recruitment, and the cereblon structures show it directly. I am less sure than Linke that Sakamoto should be left out and would like to hear whether he sees a principled way to choose between Handa and Ciulli.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first as chemically elegant and mature enough, and degradation second.
responses.response: Base editing is the closest rival and I ranked it second. My concern is the one the opening ballots raise: the 2020 CRISPR prize makes the committee's case that this is a distinct chemical invention harder to make, and Liu's unambiguous credit is offset by the independent Nishida and Kondo work. Degradation has a larger body of structural and mechanistic evidence and no recent prize on the same platform. If the committee wants a Liu-led prize, I could support it as a second part, but I would not drop degradation for it.

uncertainties: Whether a prize should be centred on PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies) alone, or also include the cereblon glue arm through Handa.
Whether Ciulli should replace Handa given structure-guided VHL work, which is a choice between the two lineages.
Whether late-stage clinical outcomes for degraders in the next few years would change the timing argument.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B014. I am a Stockholm University colleague of the secretary, Peter Brzezinski, but he is not a candidate. My own field is porous materials and electron crystallography, none of which is on this shortlist.
